messages:
alex: Heads up — we're revisiting DEK caching/KEK rotation after the vault quota spike. looking for a short, production-safe pattern for: when to call KMS (unwrap/rewrap), cache TTLs, and what RBAC + audit events we must emit. any quick takes?
pat: +1. TL;DR: cache unwrapped DEKs per-process with short access-window TTL, keep wrapped DEK persistently. avoid caching KEK material.
meera: agree but what do you mean by access-window TTL? compliance wants ability to revoke within ~10m for sensitive customers.
devin: access-window = in-memory TTL after first unwrap. e.g., unwrap -> cache {dek_id: plaintext, expires_at}. default 5m, can be overridden per-customer policy.
pat: exactly. design notes: 1) store only wrapped_dek_in_blobstore; 2) on request, if plaintext DEK not in cache -> KMS unwrap (count against quota) -> store plaintext in local process LRUCACHE keyed by (dek_id, host_id) for TTL; 3) use reachability list for long-lived workers to avoid repeated unwraps.
sre_lead: quota question — if we have N workers and high QPS, naive caching per-process multiplies KMS calls. we should use a shared cache or local LRU with sticky routing. also circuit-break if KMS 429.
pat: agree. two practical mitigations: (A) single-process per-host cache keyed by dek_id (shared memory or local redis) to reduce fanout; (B) backoff + degraded-mode: if KMS unavailable, serve from fallback cached DEK if <= short TTL, otherwise fail open only for non-sensitive routes.
meera: about RBAC — we need separate roles for unwrap vs rewrap vs admin. suggestions: kms:unwrap (runtime), kms:wrap (re-encrypt/rotate), kms:manage (create/rotate KEK). map these to service-accounts and human admin groups. audit log must include principal, ip, dek_id, operation (unwrap/wrap/rotate), and keystore_key_version.
auditor_jules: please also include a reason/trace_id in unwrap events so we can correlate to API calls in SIEM. retention for unwrap audit should be >= 1y for enterprise.
devin: small snippet for cache key & eviction:```python
cache_key = f"dek:{customer_id}:{dek_id}"
# store {plaintext, expires_at, keystore_key_version}
if now < expires_at: use plaintext
else: fetch and unwrap
```
pat: recommend defaults: access-window TTL = 300s (5m), max absolute lifetime of a cached plaintext per host = 1h (force refresh to pick up rewrap), wrapped DEK TTL in object store = unlimited (until re-encrypted).
sre_lead: also add jitter to TTLs to avoid stampedes: TTL = base * (0.8 + random()*0.4). and cold-start padding to smooth unwrap bursts.
ops-bot: :warning: KMS_QUOTA_WARNING — project-prod-us-east-1 at 2510001260: 85% of kms-unwrap QPS quota. Throttling likely if pattern unchanged.
alex: good catch ops-bot. so operational controls: sticky routing, host-level shared cache, TTL jitter, and a quota-aware unwrap wrapper that stops retries and surfaces degraded-mode.
meera: rotation story — two options: (1) KMS-driven rewrap: KMS rewrap API (if provider supports) to re-encrypt wrapped DEKs to new KEK version without unwrapping plaintext; or (2) generate new DEK and reencrypt data (more expensive). prefer (1) when available. ensure rewrap audit events record old_v -> new_v mapping.
pat: note: not all providers expose rewrap. fallback rewrap pattern: fetch wrapped_dek -> KMS unwrap -> KMS encrypt with new KEK (counts as unwrap+encrypt). schedule during low-traffic windows.
devin: for per-customer revocation we can implement short access-window TTL + revoke list: when customer is revoked, mark dek_id revoked in central store and evict from caches (publish eviction via fanout). cache eviction must be reliable and fast.
auditor_jules: please also log cache-eviction API calls and who issued them. auditors want a clear chain: admin -> revoke -> eviction -> last-access events.
sre_lead: incident response: when kms errors spike, trigger automated route failover to slower but guaranteed mode: use per-customer ephemeral DEKs (derive from KMS master via HKDF) for a limited window — but ensure derivation uses KEK material only after successful unwrap. this is more complex, log heavily.
pat: operational checklist proposal (short):
- enforce kms:unwrap / kms:wrap / kms:manage RBAC roles
- default access-window TTL 300s, per-tenant override min/max
- host-shared cache + jittered TTL + eviction fanout
- audit unwrap/wrap/rotate/evict events with principal, ip, trace_id, key_version
- rotation: prefer KMS rewrap; fallback to unwrap->encrypt with maintenance window
- quota guard: unwrap circuit-breaker + alerting

meera: can someone sketch a minimal audit entry format we can ship to SIEM?
devin: minimal JSON line we discussed:```json
{ "ts":"2510001263","principal":"infra-service@redwood","op":"kms.unwrap","dek_id":"d-abc123","keystore_key_version":"ke-2026-03-01-v3","trace_id":"t-98765","client_ip":"10.2.3.4","result":"ok" }
```
auditor_jules: add field "sensitivity":"high|normal|low" and "customer_id" for filtering. also include "action_initiator":"service|human".
alex: thanks all — pat/meera/devin: can you draft a short runbook PR for: cache config defaults, RBAC role mappings, required audit fields, and rewrap run procedure? target: RFC + ops playbook by EOD Fri. I'll open the ticket. :thumbsup:
pat: on it.
meera: will draft RBAC and compliance blurb.
devin: I'll draft the eviction & cache implementation notes and sample code.
sre_lead: I'll add the quota guard + alerting rules.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: created ticket RW-SEC-5123 with checklist and owners.
